title: Er det tid for guttetur?
subtitle: Is it time for a boys’ trip?
lead: Seven ways to say “no” became one “Ja!” The answer changed before the random index did.
paragraphs: The March 2021 website picked from seven responses to “Is it time for a boys’ trip?” “Nope,” “Helst ikke” and “Kanskje vente til pandemien er over?” gave a fairly consistent answer.
On 27 October, I replaced the list with “Ja!” The code still picked a position from zero to six. There was now an answer at position zero and nothing in the other six.
The next commit set the index to zero. The recorded commit times are 69 seconds apart. You can inspect the gap below; the larger recreation cycles through the March and October responses.

title: Retrospective.fun
subtitle: Every retro remembers the last one.
lead: A team can agree to change something, then have the same conversation a month later. Retrospective.fun keeps earlier notes and actions within reach.
paragraphs: I started Retrospective.fun in 2017 and still work on it. A retrospective is a meeting about how a team works. The useful part is often what people agree to do afterwards.

The application keeps those notes and actions available at the next session. Teams can group what people wrote, revisit earlier discussions and choose formats such as Sailboat or Six Thinking Hats, each with its own sequence.

title: NoteGame → NoteQuest
subtitle: My daughter picked up an idea I’d left unfinished.
lead: I got as far as notes on a staff and a choice of answers. My daughter built NoteQuest from that idea; she develops the game, and I look after the backend and hosting.
paragraphs: In 2023, I started NoteGame to practise reading music. It showed a note on a staff and asked you to pick the right answer. I left it unfinished.

A few years later, my daughter took up the idea and built NoteQuest using AI-assisted development. She develops the game; I provide the backend, hosting and engineering support. You can play her version now.
